# dsh-youtube-study-notes
A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) plugin that turns a YouTube link into study notes — and then gets *your*
ess (`dsh`) plugin that turns a YouTube link into study notes — and then gets *your* notes involved.
Give it a link. It pulls the video's own captions, samples the frames so it can read what was on scr
een, **stops and asks what you took from it**, and merges all three into one document.
The middle step is the point. Every other video-to-notes tool produces the same summary for everyone
. This one writes the notes you'd have written, if you'd been taking notes.
## What it does
| Step | What happens |
| 1 | **Captions** — `yt-dlp` fetches the caption track YouTube already publishes. Human-written pre

ferred, auto-generated as fallback. No ASR, no third-party transcript sites. |
| 2 | **Outline** — t

he timestamped transcript is read in full and outlined by chapter. |
| 3 | **Visual pass** *(optiona
l)* — `ffmpeg` scene-change detection samples one frame per shot; a vision model reads the on-screen

text. Catches slides, code, formulas and diagrams the narration never says out loud. |
| 4 | **Ask*

* — the agent stops and asks what *you* noticed, in your words. Type it or dictate it. |
| 5 | **Mer

ge** — transcript + on-screen evidence + your observations, into one markdown file. |
| 6 | **Save**

— `notes.md`, written beside the transcript so the evidence stays with it. |
| 7 | **Clean up** — t
he frame stills and any video file are removed; the transcript stays. |
### What it leaves on disk

The video is never kept: step 3 downloads it into a temporary directory that is deleted
when the scr

ipt exits (`--keep-video` is the only way it survives). The frame JPEGs are
removed by step 7 once `

notes.md` exists — they are derived from someone else's video and
are typically tens of megabytes, a
gainst a few kilobytes of transcript.
Kept, because it is the evidence behind every spoken claim and costs almost nothing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`cleanup.py` refuses to act on a directory that does not carry one of those markers, so
it cannot be

pointed at an unrelated folder. Pass `--keep-frames` to review the stills
yourself.

Restart the profile afterwards — bundle changes apply at boot.
Then trigger it either way:

or just ask in plain language ("get me notes from this video: …"). A link plus a request
for notes,
a summary, or study material is enough.

> **Desktop clients:** the desktop app manages its own profile. Use its **Plugins → Add
> plugin** f
low rather than the CLI, and enable the bundle when the install finishes.
## Requirements

The plugin ships no runtime code — its substance is the Skill, which drives local tools.
`dsh` does
not install these for you:
| Tool | Role | Install |

| `python3` | runs the bundled scripts (standard library only) | `brew install python3` |
| `ffmpeg`

/ `ffprobe` | audio/video probing, scene detection, frame extraction | `brew install ffmpeg` |
| `y
t-dlp` | caption listing and download | `brew install yt-dlp` |

The Skill detects missing tools, names them, and waits for your confirmation before
installing anyth

Skill detects missing tools, names them, and waits for your confirmation before
installing anything.
## Enabling the visual pass

Step 3 needs a model that accepts images, and **many model entries do not** — even ones
whose name s

ays "vision". A model is only offered images if its configuration declares
`input: [text, image]`; e

ntries otherwise default to `["text"]`, and the harness refuses
the image before attaching it with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The Skill handles this: it tries `read_image` on a single frame first. If the session
model can see

images, it reads the frames directly. If not, it delegates through the
`workflow` tool's per-agent `

provider` / `model` override, and asks you once which
image-capable model to use.

To make a model explicitly image-capable, declare it in your profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` (the file
your profile tells you to edit — not `cordis.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A profile with live reload picks this up without a restart.

> **Only declare this if the endpoint actually serves images.** Over-claiming admits an
> image the

provider then rejects mid-turn, after the message is already durable. The
> declaration is not verif

n rejects mid-turn, after the message is already durable. The
> declaration is not verified for you.

**If you skip all of this**, the plugin still works — it just produces transcript-only
notes, and sa
ys so rather than pretending it saw the screen.
## Limitations

- **Caption-less videos stop the run.** If a video publishes no caption track at all
(not even auto-

generated), step 1 reports which video failed and stops. Nothing is
invented to fill the gap. Pair t

his with a local speech-to-text plugin if you need
those covered.
- **Auto-generated captions are ro

ugh** — no punctuation, misheard proper nouns. The
skill always reports which kind it got.
- **Visio

n reads can be wrong at the character level.** A period can read as a hyphen,
`1` as `l`. Fine for p

rose, worth double-checking in code and formulas. The skill is
instructed to flag anything load-bear

ing that looks ambiguous.
- **Frame sampling sees shots, not motion.** A diagram built up over one c

ontinuous shot
yields a single frame.
- **Personal study use.** Captions, frames and notes are deriv

ed from someone else's
work. Don't republish them.
